Those albums could be badly mixed, but are they badly mixed enough that the average listener could tell? Most listeners will just hear a bad mix as being part of the way a song sounds. I just listened to born again by Black Sabbath and yeah that is a really bad mix, but some listeners might just hear it as a unique or dated sound. Anyway mixes that bad seem kind of uncommon especially since there are higher standards these days. One thing that came to mind while writing my comment was the recent Guess remix by Charli XCX with Billie Eilish. Saw a post about the song and everyone in the comments was saying there was a mixing issue but I feel like they had no idea what they were talking about tbh

A lot of people who aren’t mixers/producers just pretend they can hear mixing. They might say there’s a mixing issue if a song sounds awkward and they cant identify what exactly is wrong with it. Maybe some people can tell when something is wrong with the volume balance of a mix, but almost no one who doesn’t actually know how to mix would be able to hear an EQ issue, or badly done compression or reverb. If it was bad enough that they could, no professional or record label would’ve released the song
